source.title: KODA: Contrastive Representation Comparison and Alignment for Vision-Language Foundation Models
source.authors: Youqi Wu; Mohammad Jalali; Farzan Farnia

record.tranche_reason: The study compares embedding discrepancies and reports that the discrepancy patterns change with kernel choice and input representation; it also reports targeted alignment results. It does not test convergence as models scale.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on cross-model discrepancy structures, kernel and input-representation ablations, and alignment on selected slices. The reported retrieval results are not rows because they measure downstream retrieval rather than representational alignment. Comparisons to SPEC are not included as rows because they compare KODA with another method, rather than reporting a result about the claim itself.
record.test_reason: This is a method paper. KODA finds sample subsets clustered under one embedding but not another. It cites the Platonic Representation Hypothesis only in related work (Appendix A). It never measures global representational alignment or how alignment changes with scale, modality, seed or mapping. The ablations (kernel, RFF count, sample size) test how sensitive KODA's own discrepancy output is, not how sensitive a convergence measure is. The Table 2 alignment deliberately fine-tunes CLIP toward a target on KODA-selected slices. That induces alignment rather than measuring whether a simple map transfers representations.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that KODA localizes interpretable discrepancy clusters across unimodal and multimodal embeddings, improves over kernel-difference (SPEC) baselines, and provides slices usable for targeted alignment. Its stated limitations are the need for a shared reference dataset and an unsupervised, kernel-based notion of discrepancy.
record.recipe_differences: The paper develops constrained kernel optimization for locating discrepant sample groups and uses those groups for targeted fine-tuning; it does not reproduce or test the original scale-convergence measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: Discrepancy patterns vary with kernel function and input representation; visual stability varies with random-feature count and reference sample size.

fits_no_version.finding: Across CLIP, OpenCLIP, BLIP, SigLIP, SigLIP2 and DINOv2, KODA finds semantically coherent sample groups (e.g. baseball, surfing, bathrooms) that one model clusters tightly and another does not. The evidence is qualitative (Figs 2-3, 12-18) plus AMI 0.83 vs 0.37 for DINOv2 vs CLIP directions on FFHQ.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Even similar vision-language models organize specific semantic subsets of paired data differently (local representational discrepancies)

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning CLIP on KODA-selected slices raises its agreement with the target grouping (e.g. AMI 0.25 to 0.78 vs DINOv2 target 0.83). This narrows but does not close the gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Targeted fine-tuning on discrepancy slices can partially align one embedding's local geometry to another's

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: Alignment is evaluated on KODA-selected slices rather than general inputs; comparisons of kernel and input choices are qualitative figures without numerical effect sizes; the study does not measure convergence across model scale or capability.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: No sweep over model size or capability; no global alignment measure.
Uses image-caption pairs but never measures image-text alignment as models improve.
No linear map, stitching, relative-representation or unpaired mapping between frozen models; alignment is induced by fine-tuning on selected slices.
No test of recurring interpretable features or circuits.
No convergence score computed under different metrics, neighbour counts or out-of-distribution inputs; the ablations concern KODA's own discrepancy output.
No measurement of the global alignment level, a plateau, or causes in shared data or objectives.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 and V6 links are over-reaches. The alignment results are induced by fine-tuning and evaluated against KODA's own grouping. The ablations test KODA's own hyperparameter sensitivity, not convergence metrics. The Platonic Representation Hypothesis appears only in the related-work appendix.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over model size or capability and no measurement of convergence with scale.
Uses paired image-caption data, but does not test whether vision-language alignment rises as both models improve.
No comparison across random initializations or shared features/subspaces across seeds.
Tests targeted fine-tuning alignment on KODA-selected slices only; it does not test simple linear maps, stitching, relative representations, unpaired-data mapping, or general interchangeability.
Does not test whether interpretable features or circuits recur across models.

Tests kernel choice, modality/input representation, random-feature count, and reference sample size as factors in discrepancy patterns. Does not test out-of-distribution inputs or neighbour-count settings, and does not directly measure global convergence.
Does not measure global alignment, a convergence plateau, or the causal contribution of shared training data or objectives.

rows.subject: Aligned CLIP
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tuned CLIP on KODA-selected FFHQ samples to align local geometry with DINOv2.
rows.measure: AMI agreement between embedding-induced clusters and the KODA-discovered grouping
rows.note: The target DINOv2 value is 0.83±.006. The aligned result improves substantially over CLIP but remains below the target.
rows.check: CLIP was fine-tuned with a kernel alignment objective on KODA-selected FFHQ slices toward DINOv2. This deliberately induces alignment on selected samples; it is not a simple/linear map or stitching between frozen models, so it does not bear on V4.

rows.subject: KODA comparison: OpenCLIP vs CLIP
rows.operation_detail: Compared discrepancy directions under Gaussian and cosine similarity kernels.
rows.measure: Sample groupings in the dominant discrepancy directions
rows.note: The text states that different kernel functions produce different discrepancy patterns and groupings; the figure supplies the displayed examples.
rows.check: KODA's own sensitivity to kernel choice: which discrepancy samples it surfaces, shown only in a figure. It does not measure convergence or alignment, so it cannot show whether measured convergence depends on the metric (V6).

rows.subject: KODA comparison: SigLIP vs OpenCLIP
rows.operation_detail: Compared discrepancy directions from image-only embeddings with directions from joint image-text embeddings.
rows.measure: Coherence and semantic separation of discrepancy clusters
rows.value: Image-only embeddings produce noisier directions with weaker semantic separation.
rows.note: The study explicitly reports a qualitative difference between image-only and joint image-text results.
rows.check: Compares image-only with joint image-text inputs to KODA, judged by qualitative cluster coherence of discrepancy directions. Not an alignment/convergence measure.

rows.subject: KODA comparison: SigLIP vs OpenCLIP
rows.operation_detail: Compared discrepancy directions from image-only embeddings with directions from joint image-text embeddings.
rows.measure: Coherence and semantic separation of discrepancy clusters
rows.value: Joint image-text embeddings yield more coherent and concentrated clusters.
rows.note: The study explicitly reports a qualitative difference between image-only and joint image-text results.
rows.check: Duplicate of r9 with roles swapped; KODA output quality, not convergence.

rows.subject: KODA comparison: SigLIP vs OpenCLIP
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of joint random Fourier features used for the kernel approximation.
rows.measure: Visual coherence and separation of dominant discrepancy directions
rows.note: Across settings, the text says fewer features produce noisier directions and more features yield progressively more coherent and stable groupings.
rows.check: Random Fourier feature count is KODA's approximation hyperparameter. This is a method-stability ablation, not a similarity-measure setting for convergence.
